context_title:
Build a complete, production ready biomolecular structure prediction system implemented in a single Julia source file named structure_prediction.jl. Every function, struct, and constant described below must be fully implemented — no stubs, no placeholders, no TODO comments, no empty bodies, no simplified logic. The file must be executable end to end.

   

   Top level file organization

The file must be organized in the following order of sections, each clearly delimited by a comment block:

1. Imports and package declarations
2. Constants
3. CIF parser
4. Structure representation
5. Chemical components dictionary
6. Geometry primitives
7. MSA processing
8. Template processing
9. Featurization pipeline
10. Neural network modules
11. Evoformer
12. Diffusion head
13. Confidence head
14. Full model
15. Data pipeline
16. Post processing and main entry point

   

   Section 1: Imports

Import the following Julia standard library and registered package modules at the top of the file:

julia
using LinearAlgebra, Statistics, Random, Dates, Printf
using JSON3, CodecZstd, Tar


If Flux is available, import it. Otherwise implement all neural network operations using plain Julia arrays and LinearAlgebra. All neural network forward passes must use Float32 arithmetic throughout.

   Section 3: CIF Parser

Implement a complete mmCIF/CIF parser.

  struct CifDict   — wraps Dict{String,Vector{String}} plus a data_name::String field. Implement Base.getindex, Base.get, Base.haskey, Base.keys, Base.length, Base.iterate delegating to the inner dict.

  function tokenize_cif(s::AbstractString)::Vector{String}   — tokenize a CIF string into tokens. Handle:
  Whitespace delimited bare tokens.
  Single quoted strings '...' (may span one line, '' is not an escape).
  Double quoted strings "...".
  Semicolon text blocks: a line starting with ; begins a text block terminated by a line whose first character is ;.
  Comments starting with   (skip to end of line).
  Return all tokens as a Vector{String} with quotes stripped.

  function from_string(cif_string::Union{String,Vector{UInt8}})::CifDict   — parse a single block CIF string:
  Call tokenize_cif.
  Expect the first token to start with data_; store the block name.
  Parse key value pairs: token starting with _ is a key, next token is its value (stored as Vector{String} of length 1).
  Parse loop_ blocks: collect all _ prefixed keys, then read values in row major order until the next _ prefixed token or loop_ or data_ or end of tokens.
  Return a CifDict.

  function parse_multi_data_cif(cif_string::Union{String,Vector{UInt8}})::Dict{String,CifDict}   — split on data_ boundaries and call from_string on each block. Return a Dict keyed by block name.

  function extract_loop_as_list(cif::CifDict, prefix::String)::Vector{Dict{String,String}}   — find all keys starting with prefix, zip their value vectors into a list of row dicts.

  function extract_loop_as_dict(cif::CifDict, prefix::String, index::String)::Dict{String,Dict{String,String}}   — same as above but keyed by the value of the index column.

  function to_string(cif::CifDict)::String   — serialize back to valid CIF format. Use loop_ for all multi valued fields. Wrap values containing spaces or special characters in single quotes.

  function int_id_to_str_id(num::Int)::String   — encode positive integer as reverse spreadsheet string: 1→"A", 2→"B", ..., 26→"Z", 27→"AA", 28→"BA", 29→"CA", ..., 53→"AAA". Algorithm: num  = 1; result = []; while num >= 0; push!(result, Char(num % 26 + Int('A'))); num = num ÷ 26   1; end; join(result).

  function str_id_to_int_id(str_id::String)::Int   — inverse of above.

  function get_release_date(cif::CifDict)::Union{Date,Nothing}   — extract _pdbx_database_status.recvd_initial_deposition_date or _entry.id date; parse as Date(s, dateformat"yyyy mm dd"); return nothing if absent or unparseable.

  function get_internal_to_author_chain_id_map(cif::CifDict)::Dict{String,String}   — zip _atom_site.label_asym_id and _atom_site.auth_asym_id into a dict, deduplicating.

   

   Section 4: Structure Representation

  struct ChainsTable   with fields: key::Vector{Int64}, id::Vector{String}, type::Vector{String}, auth_id::Vector{String}, entity_id::Vector{String}, entity_desc::Vector{String}.

  struct ResiduesTable   with fields: key::Vector{Int64}, chain_key::Vector{Int64}, id::Vector{Int32}, name::Vector{String}, auth_seq_id::Vector{String}, insertion_code::Vector{String}, is_missing::Vector{Bool}.

  struct AtomsTable   with fields: key::Vector{Int64}, chain_key::Vector{Int64}, res_key::Vector{Int64}, name::Vector{String}, element::Vector{String}, x::Vector{Float32}, y::Vector{Float32}, z::Vector{Float32}, b_factor::Vector{Float32}, occupancy::Vector{Float32}.

  struct BondsTable   with fields: key::Vector{Int64}, from_atom_key::Vector{Int64}, dest_atom_key::Vector{Int64}, type::Vector{String}, role::Vector{String}.

  struct Structure   with fields: name::String, release_date::Union{Date,Nothing}, resolution::Union{Float64,Nothing}, structure_method::Union{String,Nothing}, chains::ChainsTable, residues::ResiduesTable, atoms::AtomsTable, bonds::BondsTable.

  function from_mmcif(mmcif_string::Union{String,Vector{UInt8}}; name::Union{String,Nothing}=nothing, fix_mse_residues::Bool=false, fix_arginines::Bool=false, fix_unknown_dna::Bool=false, include_water::Bool=false, include_other::Bool=false, include_bonds::Bool=false, model_id::Union{Int,Symbol}=:first)::Structure  

Full implementation:
1. Parse with from_string.
2. Extract _atom_site columns: label_asym_id, label_seq_id, label_comp_id, label_atom_id, type_symbol, Cartn_x, Cartn_y, Cartn_z, B_iso_or_equiv, occupancy, label_alt_id, pdbx_PDB_model_num, auth_asym_id, auth_seq_id, pdbx_PDB_ins_code.
3. Filter by model_id: if :first, keep only rows where pdbx_PDB_model_num equals the first unique value; if an integer, keep rows matching that value; if :all, keep all.
4. Resolve alternate locations: for each (asym_id, seq_id, atom_id) group, keep the row with the highest occupancy; break ties by first occurrence. Remove rows with non empty label_alt_id that were not selected.
5. Build ChainsTable from _struct_asym, _entity, _entity_poly tables. Each unique label_asym_id in _atom_site becomes a chain. Set type from _entity_poly.type (for polymers) or _entity.type (for non polymers). Filter out water chains unless include_water=true. Filter out other chains unless include_other=true.
6. Build ResiduesTable: for polymer chains, use _entity_poly_seq to include missing residues (set is_missing=true). For non polymer chains, one residue per unique (label_asym_id, label_seq_id, label_comp_id) group.
7. Build AtomsTable from filtered _atom_site rows, assigning chain_key and res_key by lookup.
8. If fix_mse_residues: for atoms with res_name="MSE" and atom_name="SE", set element="S" and atom_name="SD".
9. If fix_arginines: for ARG residues, if the distance from CD to NH1 > distance from CD to NH2, swap NH1↔NH2 (and HH11,HH12 ↔ HH21,HH22).
10. If fix_unknown_dna: for DNA chains, rename residue N to DN.
11. If include_bonds: build BondsTable from _struct_conn table, mapping partner atom identifiers to atom keys.
12. Return Structure.

  function to_mmcif_dict(struc::Structure)::CifDict   — serialize to a complete mmCIF dict including _atom_site, _entity, _entity_poly, _entity_poly_seq, _struct_asym, _struct_conn (if bonds present), _cell, _symmetry, _entry tables.

  function filter_structure(struc::Structure; chain_ids::Union{Vector{String},Nothing}=nothing, res_names::Union{Set{String},Nothing}=nothing, atom_names::Union{Set{String},Nothing}=nothing, chain_types::Union{Set{String},Nothing}=nothing)::Structure   — filter chains/residues/atoms by the given criteria, rebuilding all key arrays.

  function copy_and_update_coords(struc::Structure, coords::Matrix{Float32})::Structure   — return a new Structure with atoms.x, atoms.y, atoms.z replaced by columns of coords (shape (N,3)).

  function chain_single_letter_sequence(struc::Structure, chain_key::Int64)::String   — return the one letter sequence for a polymer chain using THREE_LETTER_TO_ONE, substituting 'X' for unknowns.

   

   Section 5: Chemical Components Dictionary

  struct ChemCompEntry   with fields: type::String, name::String, pdbx_synonyms::String, formula::String, formula_weight::String, mon_nstd_flag::String, pdbx_smiles::Union{String,Nothing}.

  struct Ccd   wrapping data::Dict{String,Dict{String,Vector{String}}}. Implement Base.getindex, Base.get, Base.haskey, Base.keys, Base.length.

  const _CCD_CACHE = Ref{Union{Ccd,Nothing}}(nothing)   and   const _CCD_CACHE_PATH = Ref{String}("")  .

  function load_ccd(ccd_cif_path::String)::Ccd   — if _CCD_CACHE_PATH[] == ccd_cif_path and _CCD_CACHE[] !== nothing, return cached value. Otherwise parse the multi block CIF file at ccd_cif_path (which may be gzip compressed; detect by .gz extension and decompress with GZip or CodecZlib if available, otherwise require uncompressed). Convert each block to Dict{String,Vector{String}} via to_dict. Store in _CCD_CACHE[] and _CCD_CACHE_PATH[]. Return the Ccd.

  function Ccd(; ccd_cif_path::Union{String,Nothing}=nothing, user_ccd::Union{String,Nothing}=nothing)::Ccd   — load from ccd_cif_path (or a default path from the CCD_PATH environment variable if nothing). If user_ccd is provided, parse it as a multi block CIF and merge into the dict (user entries override existing entries).

  function get_chem_comp_entry(ccd::Ccd, comp_id::String)::Union{ChemCompEntry,Nothing}   — look up comp_id in ccd.data, extract _chem_comp.type, _chem_comp.name, _chem_comp.pdbx_synonyms, _chem_comp.formula, _chem_comp.formula_weight, _chem_comp.mon_nstd_flag, _chem_comp_atom.pdbx_model_Cartn_x_ideal (to detect if ideal coords exist), and _pdbx_chem_comp_descriptor SMILES. Return ChemCompEntry or nothing.

  function type_symbol(ccd::Ccd, comp_id::String, atom_name::String)::String   — look up _chem_comp_atom.type_symbol for the given atom in the component. Return "X" if not found.

  function get_all_atoms_in_entry(ccd::Ccd, comp_id::String)::Vector{String}   — return _chem_comp_atom.atom_id values for the component, excluding hydrogen atoms (where _chem_comp_atom.type_symbol is "H" or "D").

   

   Section 6: Geometry Primitives

All structs hold batched arrays of arbitrary shape. Operations broadcast element wise.

  struct Vec3Array   with fields x::AbstractArray{Float32}, y::AbstractArray{Float32}, z::AbstractArray{Float32}.

Implement:
  Base.:+(a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = Vec3Array(a.x+b.x, a.y+b.y, a.z+b.z)
  Base.: (a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = Vec3Array(a.x b.x, a.y b.y, a.z b.z)
  Base.: (v::Vec3Array) = Vec3Array( v.x,  v.y,  v.z)
  Base.: (s::Real, v::Vec3Array) = Vec3Array(s v.x, s v.y, s v.z)
  Base.: (v::Vec3Array, s::Real) = s   v
  dot3(a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = a.x. b.x .+ a.y. b.y .+ a.z. b.z
  cross3(a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = Vec3Array(a.y. b.z .  a.z. b.y, a.z. b.x .  a.x. b.z, a.x. b.y .  a.y. b.x)
  norm3(v::Vec3Array) = sqrt.(v.x.^2 .+ v.y.^2 .+ v.z.^2 .+ 1f 12)
  normalized3(v::Vec3Array) = (n = norm3(v); Vec3Array(v.x./n, v.y./n, v.z./n))
  square_euclidean_distance(a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = (d=a b; d.x.^2 .+ d.y.^2 .+ d.z.^2)
  euclidean_distance(a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = sqrt.(square_euclidean_distance(a,b) .+ 1f 12)
  dihedral_angle(a,b,c,d) — compute using the standard formula: b1=b a; b2=c b; b3=d c; n1=cross3(b1,b2); n2=cross3(b2,b3); m1=cross3(n1,normalized3(b2)); atan.(dot3(m1,n2), dot3(n1,n2)).

  struct Rot3Array   with fields xx,xy,xz,yx,yy,yz,zx,zy,zz::AbstractArray{Float32}.

Implement:
  apply_rot(r::Rot3Array, v::Vec3Array) = Vec3Array(r.xx. v.x .+ r.xy. v.y .+ r.xz. v.z, r.yx. v.x .+ r.yy. v.y .+ r.yz. v.z, r.zx. v.x .+ r.zy. v.y .+ r.zz. v.z)
  compose_rot(a::Rot3Array, b::Rot3Array) — full 3×3 matrix multiplication broadcasting over batch dims.
  inverse_rot(r::Rot3Array) = Rot3Array(r.xx,r.yx,r.zx, r.xy,r.yy,r.zy, r.xz,r.yz,r.zz)
  rot_from_two_vectors(e0::Vec3Array, e1::Vec3Array)::Rot3Array — Gram Schmidt: u0=normalized3(e0); u1=normalized3(e1   dot3(e1,u0). u0); u2=cross3(u0,u1); Rot3Array(u0.x,u1.x,u2.x, u0.y,u1.y,u2.y, u0.z,u1.z,u2.z).
  identity_rot3(sz::Tuple)::Rot3Array — ones on diagonal, zeros off diagonal, all of shape sz.

  struct Rigid3Array   with fields rotation::Rot3Array, translation::Vec3Array.

Implement:
  compose_rigid(a::Rigid3Array, b::Rigid3Array) = Rigid3Array(compose_rot(a.rotation, b.rotation), apply_rot(a.rotation, b.translation) + a.translation)
  inverse_rigid(r::Rigid3Array) = (inv_rot = inverse_rot(r.rotation); Rigid3Array(inv_rot,  apply_rot(inv_rot, r.translation)))
  apply_rigid(r::Rigid3Array, p::Vec3Array) = apply_rot(r.rotation, p) + r.translation
  identity_rigid3(sz::Tuple)::Rigid3Array
  rigid_from_point_alignment(mobile::Matrix{Float32}, target::Matrix{Float32})::Rigid3Array — SVD based alignment: center both point sets, compute F = target_centered'   mobile_centered, SVD decompose U,S,Vt = svd(F), handle reflection with d = sign(det(U Vt)), rotation R = U   diagm([1,1,d])   Vt, translation t = target_mean   R   mobile_mean. Return as Rigid3Array with scalar (0 dim) arrays.

   

   Section 7: MSA Processing

  struct MsaToolResult   with fields target_sequence::String, e_value::Float64, a3m::String, tblout::Union{String,Nothing}.

  struct Msa   with fields query_sequence::String, chain_poly_type::String, sequences::Vector{String}, descriptions::Vector{String}.

  function Msa(query_sequence::String, chain_poly_type::String, sequences::Vector{String}, descriptions::Vector{String}; deduplicate::Bool=true)::Msa  :
  If deduplicate: build a Set{String} of seen sequences (with lowercase letters removed via filter(isuppercase, seq) or replace(seq, r"[a z]"=>"")). Iterate (seq,desc) pairs; add to output only if the stripped sequence is not yet seen.
  Ensure sequences is non empty; if empty after dedup, set to [query_sequence] and descriptions to ["Original query"].
  Verify sequences[1] is feature equivalent to query_sequence (same uppercase letters after stripping lowercase).

  function parse_fasta(fasta_string::String)::Vector{Tuple{String,String}}   — split on >, parse description (first line after >) and sequence (remaining lines joined, stripping whitespace).

  function from_a3m(a3m_str::String, query_sequence::String, chain_poly_type::String)::Msa   — call parse_fasta, construct Msa.

  function to_a3m(msa::Msa)::String   — serialize to A3M: for each (seq,desc) pair, write >desc\n then seq\n.

  function convert_a3m_to_stockholm(a3m_sequences::Vector{String})::Vector{String}  :
  Find max length element.
  Process column by column: if any sequence has a lowercase character at the current position, it is an insertion column — sequences with a lowercase char emit it uppercased, others emit  . Otherwise it is a match column — all sequences emit their current character (or   if exhausted, which is an error for valid A3M).
  Return the Stockholm format sequences (all same length).

  function extract_msa_features(msa_sequences::Vector{String}, chain_poly_type::String)::Tuple{Matrix{Int32},Matrix{Int32}}  :
  Determine the residue to index mapping from chain_poly_type (use PROTEIN_TYPE_INDEX, RNA_TYPE_INDEX, or DNA_TYPE_INDEX).
  For each sequence: iterate characters; uppercase chars are match positions (encode to integer); lowercase chars are insertions (increment deletion counter for the next match position).
  Return (msa_array, deletion_matrix) both of shape (num_seq, num_res).

  function compute_msa_profile(msa::Matrix{Int32}, num_residue_types::Int)::Matrix{Float64}  :
  Shape: (num_res, num_residue_types).
  For each position and each sequence, increment profile[pos, residue_code+1] by 1/num_seq.
  Return the profile matrix.

  function parse_sequence_identifier(identifier::String)::String   — search for the pattern (tr|sp)\|[A Z0 9]+\|[A Z0 9]+_([A Z0 9]+) and return the species part (after _). Return "" if not found.

  function get_species_ids(descriptions::Vector{String})::Vector{String}   — map parse_sequence_identifier over descriptions.

   

   Section 8: Template Processing

  struct Hit   with fields: pdb_id::String, auth_chain_id::String, hmmsearch_sequence::String, structure_sequence::String, unresolved_res_indices::Union{Vector{Int},Nothing}, query_sequence::String, start_index::Int, end_index::Int, full_length::Int, release_date::Date, chain_poly_type::String.

  function parse_hmmsearch_a3m(a3m_str::String, query_sequence::String, chain_poly_type::String, max_template_date::Union{Date,Nothing})::Vector{Hit}  :
  Parse A3M with parse_fasta.
  Skip the first sequence (query).
  For each hit sequence: parse the description to extract PDB ID, chain ID, start index, end index, full length, release date (format YYYY MM DD).
  Filter out hits with release_date > max_template_date if max_template_date is not nothing.
  Build query_to_hit_mapping from the gapped alignment (map query positions to hit positions, skipping gaps).
  Return Vector{Hit}.

  function realign_hit_to_structure(; hit_sequence::String, hit_start_index::Int, hit_end_index::Int, full_length::Int, structure_sequence::String, query_to_hit_mapping::Dict{Int,Int})::Dict{Int,Int}  :
  Strip gaps from hit_sequence to get the gapless hit.
  Align the gapless hit to structure_sequence using a simple O(n) scan: find the longest common subsequence prefix starting from hit_start_index in the structure.
  Build and return a new query_to_structure_mapping.

  struct Templates   with fields query_sequence::String, hits::Vector{Hit}.

  function get_polymer_features(templates::Templates, structure_store, ccd::Ccd, max_templates::Int, max_template_date::Union{Date,Nothing})::Dict{String,Array}  :
  Select up to max_templates hits (already filtered by date).
  For each hit: load the mmCIF from structure_store, parse with from_mmcif, extract atom positions for the hit chain, build the (num_res, 37, 3) atom position array and (num_res, 37) mask using ATOM37_ORDER.
  Pad to max_templates with zeros.
  Return dict with keys "template_aatype" (Int32, shape (max_templates, num_res)), "template_all_atom_positions" (Float32, shape (max_templates, num_res, 37, 3)), "template_all_atom_mask" (Float32, shape (max_templates, num_res, 37)), "template_domain_names" (Vector{String}), "template_sequence" (Vector{String}), "template_sum_probs" (Float32, shape (max_templates,)).

   

   Section 9: Featurization Pipeline

  function from_json(json_str::String)::FoldingInput   — parse the JSON object. The JSON format has keys "name", "sequences" (array of objects each with one of "protein", "rna", "dna", "ligand" keys), "modelSeeds" (array of ints), "bondedAtomPairs" (optional), "userCCD" (optional string). Each sequence object has "id" (string or array of strings), "sequence" (for polymers), "modifications" (for PTMs), "unpairedMsa", "pairedMsa", "templates" (for proteins), "ccdCodes" or "smiles" (for ligands). All modules are implemented as mutable structs with a weight and optional bias field. Forward passes are implemented as (module)(input...) callable structs. All weights are Array{Float32}. No automatic differentiation is required for inference; implement only the forward pass.

function (t::Transition)(x::Array{Float32})::Array{Float32}:
  x = t.norm(x)
  a = swish.(t.linear1(x)) where swish(x) = x .  sigmoid.(x) and sigmoid(x) = 1f0 ./ (1f0 .+ exp.( x)).
  b = t.linear2(x)
  return t.linear3(a .  b)

  mutable struct TriangleMultiplication   with fields norm_input::LayerNorm, left_projection::Linear, right_projection::Linear, left_gate::Linear, right_gate::Linear, output_projection::Linear, output_gate::Linear, norm_output::LayerNorm, equation::String.

function (tm::TriangleMultiplication)(pair::Array{Float32,3}, mask::Matrix{Float32})::Array{Float32,3}:
  pair = tm.norm_input(pair) — shape (N, N, c_z).
  left = sigmoid.(tm.left_gate(pair)) .  tm.left_projection(pair) — shape (N, N, c).
  right = sigmoid.(tm.right_gate(pair)) .  tm.right_projection(pair) — shape (N, N, c).
  Apply mask: left . = mask[:,:,:] (broadcast).
  If equation == "kjc,kic >ijc" (incoming): result[i,j,c] = sum_k left[k,j,c]   right[k,i,c] — implement as einsum or equivalent batched matrix multiply: result = permutedims(left, (2,3,1))   permutedims(right, (1,3,2)) reshaped appropriately.
  If equation == "ikc,jkc >ijc" (outgoing): result[i,j,c] = sum_k left[i,k,c]   right[j,k,c].
  result = tm.norm_output(result)
  return sigmoid.(tm.output_gate(pair)) .  tm.output_projection(result)

  mutable struct GridSelfAttention   with fields norm::LayerNorm, q_projection::Linear, k_projection::Linear, v_projection::Linear, output_projection::Linear, gating::Linear, num_heads::Int, head_dim::Int.

function (gsa::GridSelfAttention)(pair::Array{Float32,3}, mask::Matrix{Float32})::Array{Float32,3}:
  Row wise attention: for each row i, compute attention over all j positions using pair[i,:,:] as queries/keys/values, with pair bias from pair[i,:,:]. Then column wise attention: for each column j, compute attention over all i positions.
  Use scaled dot product attention: scores = Q   K' / sqrt(head_dim), add pair bias, softmax, multiply by V.
  Apply gating: output = sigmoid.(gating(pair)) .  output.
  Return updated pair representation.

function (opm::OuterProductMean)(msa::Array{Float32,3}, mask::Matrix{Float32})::Array{Float32,3}:
  msa = opm.norm(msa) — shape (num_seq, num_res, c_m).
  left = opm.left_projection(msa) — shape (num_seq, num_res, c).
  right = opm.right_projection(msa) — shape (num_seq, num_res, c).
  Apply mask: left . = mask[:,:,1].
  Outer product mean: result[i,j,c1,c2] = mean_s(left[s,i,c1]   right[s,j,c2]) — implement as (left'   right) / num_seq reshaped to (num_res, num_res, c c).
  return opm.output_projection(result)

function (pf::PairFormerIteration)(pair::Array{Float32,3}, single::Union{Array{Float32,2},Nothing}, pair_mask::Matrix{Float32})::Tuple:

  struct Vec3Array   with fields x::AbstractArray{Float32}, y::AbstractArray{Float32}, z::AbstractArray{Float32}.

Implement:
  Base.:+(a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = Vec3Array(a.x+b.x, a.y+b.y, a.z+b.z)
  Base.: (a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = Vec3Array(a.x b.x, a.y b.y, a.z b.z)

  square_euclidean_distance(a::Vec3Array, b::Vec3Array) = (d=a b; d.x.^2 .+ d.y.^2 .+ d.z.^2)

Full implementation:
1.   Tokenization  : iterate chains in order. For each ProteinChain or RnaChain or DnaChain, emit one token per residue. For each Ligand, emit one token per heavy atom (from CCD or SMILES). Assign chain_index, residue_index, token_index, entity_id, sym_id, num_sym, is_protein/rna/dna/ligand flags, aatype (integer residue type).
2.   MSA features  : for each protein chain, parse paired_msa and unpaired_msa A3M strings into Msa objects. Call extract_msa_features. Compute profile with compute_msa_profile. Pair MSA rows across chains by species ID (see create_paired_features below). Merge paired and unpaired MSA. Deduplicate unpaired against paired if resolve_msa_overlaps. Concatenate across chains, padding shorter MSAs with gap rows.
3.   Template features  : for each protein chain, call get_polymer_features on its templates field.
4.   Reference structure  : for each token, generate 3D reference atom positions. For polymer residues, use ideal coordinates from CCD (_chem_comp_atom.model_Cartn_x/y/z or _chem_comp_atom.pdbx_model_Cartn_x_ideal/y_ideal/z_ideal). For ligands, use CCD ideal coordinates. If ideal coordinates are absent, generate a distance geometry conformer: place atoms at random positions, then iteratively minimize violations of distance bounds derived from bond lengths and angles from CCD _chem_comp_bond table (100 iterations of gradient descent with step size 0.1). Store positions as (num_tokens, max_atoms_per_token, 3) Float32 array.
5.   Bucket padding  : if buckets is provided, find the smallest bucket ≥ num_tokens; pad all token dimension arrays to that size. Raise an error if num_tokens exceeds the largest bucket.
6. Return one Batch per rng_seed (all seeds share the same features; the seed is used only during diffusion sampling).

  function create_relative_encoding(token_features::TokenFeatures, max_relative_idx::Int=32, max_relative_chain::Int=2)::Array{Float32,3}  :
  For each pair (i,j) of tokens, compute:
    rel_pos = clamp(residue_index[j]   residue_index[i],  max_relative_idx, max_relative_idx) + max_relative_idx (one hot, 2 max_relative_idx+1 dims).
    rel_chain = clamp(chain_index[j]   chain_index[i],  max_relative_chain, max_relative_chain) + max_relative_chain (one hot, 2 max_relative_chain+1 dims).
    same_chain = Float32(chain_index[i] == chain_index[j]) (1 dim).
    same_entity = Float32(entity_id[i] == entity_id[j]) (1 dim).
  Concatenate all one hot vectors for each pair into a (num_tokens, num_tokens, D) array where D = (2 max_relative_idx+1) + (2 max_relative_chain+1) + 2.

  function create_paired_features(chains_msa::Vector{Msa}, max_paired_sequences::Int=600, max_hits_per_species::Int=1)::Vector{Msa}  :
  For each chain, build a Dict{String,Vector{Int}} mapping species ID to row indices.
  Find species present in all chains simultaneously.
  For each such species, take up to max_hits_per_species rows from each chain.
  Align rows across chains so that row n in chain k corresponds to the same species as row n in chain k'. Pad chains with fewer hits for that species with gap rows.
  Limit total paired rows to max_paired_sequences.
  Return new Msa objects with paired sequences prepended.

   

   Section 10: Neural Network Modules

All modules are implemented as mutable structs with a weight and optional bias field. Forward passes are implemented as (module)(input...) callable structs. All weights are Array{Float32}. No automatic differentiation is required for inference; implement only the forward pass.

  mutable struct LayerNorm   with fields weight::Vector{Float32}, bias::Vector{Float32}, eps::Float32, upcast::Bool.

function (ln::LayerNorm)(x::Array{Float32})::Array{Float32}:
  If upcast and eltype is not Float32, cast to Float32.
  Compute mean and variance over the last dimension.
  Normalize: (x .  mean) ./ sqrt.(var .+ ln.eps).
  Scale and shift: ln.weight .  normalized .+ ln.bias (broadcast over batch dims).

  mutable struct Linear   with fields weight::Matrix{Float32}, bias::Union{Vector{Float32},Nothing}.

function (lin::Linear)(x::Array{Float32})::Array{Float32}:
  Reshape x to (in_dim, :), multiply lin.weight   x_2d, reshape back.
  Add lin.bias if present.

  mutable struct Transition   with fields norm::LayerNorm, linear1::Linear, linear2::Linear, linear3::Linear.

function (t::Transition)(x::Array{Float32})::Array{Float32}:
  x = t.norm(x)
  a = swish.(t.linear1(x)) where swish(x) = x .  sigmoid.(x) and sigmoid(x) = 1f0 ./ (1f0 .+ exp.( x)).
  b = t.linear2(x)
  return t.linear3(a .  b)

  mutable struct TriangleMultiplication   with fields norm_input::LayerNorm, left_projection::Linear, right_projection::Linear, left_gate::Linear, right_gate::Linear, output_projection::Linear, output_gate::Linear, norm_output::LayerNorm, equation::String.

function (tm::TriangleMultiplication)(pair::Array{Float32,3}, mask::Matrix{Float32})::Array{Float32,3}:
  pair = tm.norm_input(pair) — shape (N, N, c_z).
  left = sigmoid.(tm.left_gate(pair)) .  tm.left_projection(pair) — shape (N, N, c).
  right = sigmoid.(tm.right_gate(pair)) .  tm.right_projection(pair) — shape (N, N, c).
  Apply mask: left . = mask[:,:,:] (broadcast).
  If equation == "kjc,kic >ijc" (incoming): result[i,j,c] = sum_k left[k,j,c]   right[k,i,c] — implement as einsum or equivalent batched matrix multiply: result = permutedims(left, (2,3,1))   permutedims(right, (1,3,2)) reshaped appropriately.
  If equation == "ikc,jkc >ijc" (outgoing): result[i,j,c] = sum_k left[i,k,c]   right[j,k,c].
  result = tm.norm_output(result)
  return sigmoid.(tm.output_gate(pair)) .  tm.output_projection(result)

  mutable struct GridSelfAttention   with fields norm::LayerNorm, q_projection::Linear, k_projection::Linear, v_projection::Linear, output_projection::Linear, gating::Linear, num_heads::Int, head_dim::Int.

function (gsa::GridSelfAttention)(pair::Array{Float32,3}, mask::Matrix{Float32})::Array{Float32,3}:
  Row wise attention: for each row i, compute attention over all j positions using pair[i,:,:] as queries/keys/values, with pair bias from pair[i,:,:]. Then column wise attention: for each column j, compute attention over all i positions.
  Use scaled dot product attention: scores = Q   K' / sqrt(head_dim), add pair bias, softmax, multiply by V.
  Apply gating: output = sigmoid.(gating(pair)) .  output.
  Return updated pair representation.

  mutable struct OuterProductMean   with fields norm::LayerNorm, left_projection::Linear, right_projection::Linear, output_projection::Linear.

function (opm::OuterProductMean)(msa::Array{Float32,3}, mask::Matrix{Float32})::Array{Float32,3}:
  msa = opm.norm(msa) — shape (num_seq, num_res, c_m).
  left = opm.left_projection(msa) — shape (num_seq, num_res, c).
  right = opm.right_projection(msa) — shape (num_seq, num_res, c).
  Apply mask: left . = mask[:,:,1].
  Outer product mean: result[i,j,c1,c2] = mean_s(left[s,i,c1]   right[s,j,c2]) — implement as (left'   right) / num_seq reshaped to (num_res, num_res, c c).
  return opm.output_projection(result)

  mutable struct MSARowAttentionWithPairBias   with fields norm_msa::LayerNorm, norm_pair::LayerNorm, q_projection::Linear, k_projection::Linear, v_projection::Linear, pair_bias::Linear, output_projection::Linear, gating::Linear, num_heads::Int, head_dim::Int.

function (attn::MSARowAttentionWithPairBias)(msa::Array{Float32,3}, pair::Array{Float32,3}, msa_mask::Matrix{Float32})::Array{Float32,3}:

function (block::DiffusionTransformerBlock)(x::Array{Float32,2}, conditioning::Array{Float32,2}, pair_bias::Union{Array{Float32,3},Nothing}=nothing)::Array{Float32,2}:
  Compute AdaLN zero scale and shift from conditioning: scale = block.ada_ln_scale(conditioning), shift = block.ada_ln_shift(conditioning).
  x_norm = block.norm1(x) .  (1f0 .+ scale) .+ shift
  Compute Q, K, V from x_norm. Add pair_bias to attention logits if provided. Apply scaled dot product attention. Apply gating. Add residual.
  x = x .+ block.transition(block.norm2(x))
  Return x.

  function noise_embeddings(sigma::AbstractArray{Float32})::AbstractArray{Float32}  :
  log_sigma = (1f0/4f0) .  log.(sigma)
  Multiply by fixed weight matrix W of shape (1, 128) (initialized from randn(Float32, 128)   1.0 at module load time, stored as a module level const) and add fixed bias b of shape (128,).
  Return cos.(2f0   Float32(π) .  (log_sigma .  W .+ b)) — shape (batch, 256) (concatenate cos of both halves).

Note: the fixed weights and biases for noise embeddings must be stored as module level constants initialized with a fixed seed (Random.seed!(42); const NOISE_EMB_W = randn(Float32, 128); const NOISE_EMB_B = randn(Float32, 128)) so they are deterministic.

  function (evo::Evoformer)(batch::Batch, is_training::Bool)::NamedTuple  :
1. Build MSA feature tensor: one hot encode batch.msa.rows (shape (num_seq, num_res, num_residue_types)), concatenate deletion matrix features (shape (num_seq, num_res, 1)). Project to msa_channel.
2. Build pair representation: compute create_relative_encoding(batch.token_features), project to pair_channel. Add template embedding output.
3. Build single representation: compute create_target_feat(batch), project to seq_channel.
4. Crop MSA to config.num_msa rows if needed (random crop during training, first rows during inference).
5. Run MSA stack: for each EvoformerIteration, update (msa, pair, single).
6. Run PairFormer stack: for each PairFormerIteration, update (pair, single).
7. Return (msa=msa[1,:,:], pair=pair, single=single) — take only the first MSA row (query) for the MSA output.

function (te::TemplateEmbedding)(batch::Batch, pair::Array{Float32,3})::Array{Float32,3}:
1. For each template: compute distogram features from batch.templates.all_atom_positions (bin pairwise Cβ distances into 39 bins from 3.25Å to 50.75Å, 1.5Å width). Compute backbone frame features (unit vectors from N→CA and CA→C). Concatenate with template aatype one hot. Project to num_channels.
2. Run num_pairformer_layers PairFormer iterations.
3. Average over templates (weighted by batch.templates.sum_probs, masked by valid templates).
4. Project to pair_channel and return.
